subject: 🏃 Saturday — Walk + B2B Prep (Wk 2)
html:
Tomorrow: 45–60 min brisk walk. No run. Flat terrain, 15–17 min/mi pace, no hills. This replaces the original 5K shakeout — walking gives you the same leg flush without eccentric loading or junk fatigue heading into Sunday's race. Your legs got three real stimulus days this week (Tue VO2, Wed heavy squat, Thu progression with 19:30 in Z4) and a clean bodyweight session today — they've earned easy mileage, not more pounding.

B2B race prep tonight: Lay out your race kit and pre-check all 3 Maurten Gel 100 pouches — one-handed dry-tear test on each. Set aside any that don't open clean and replace them. You switched to Maurten after the C30 packaging disaster on Thursday, so this is the first race-day use. No surprises tomorrow morning.

Sunday Bay to Breakers plan (quick preview): 10 mi total. Miles 1–6 @ 8:30–8:45 steady. Miles 6–9.3 @ 7:35–7:45 MP — cap at 7:35, do not let race-day adrenaline pull you to 7:10. Hayes Hill (mi 2) by effort, not pace. Fueling: banana + Maurten Drink Mix 160 (40 g) 60 min pre-start, 4 oz water 15 min pre-gun. Maurten Gel 100 at miles 3, 5.5, and 8 (75 g over ~80 min, ~55 g/hr). Water at every aid station.

Knee veto rule for Sunday: If you wake up Saturday night or Sunday morning at 2+ on the 5-point scale, run the entire 10 mi easy at 9:00 and skip the fast finish. The knee has been 1/5 across every session this week — track, heavy squat, threshold progression, bodyweight stability — so the odds are good, but the rule stands.

Focus cue: Tonight is about prep and sleep, not training. Hydrate well, get to bed by 10, set your alarm for race-morning logistics. The walk tomorrow is a formality — Sunday is the workout that matters this week.

Context: Week 2 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation. Bay to Breakers is your first fast-finish stimulus and the first real race-day rehearsal of the Maurten protocol. 10 weeks to SF Marathon.
